title: Discovery — Northwind Analytics x DL Academy

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Thanks for making the time, Priya, Marco. I'd love to understand what prompted you to look at a data and AI literacy program right now.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Sure. We've grown the data team to about 40 people, but the wider business — product, ops, finance — can't really interpret the dashboards we ship. Decisions still get made on gut feel.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: That's a really common pattern. When a decision gets made on gut feel and it goes wrong, what does that actually cost you?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Last quarter we over-ordered inventory because someone misread a forecast. That was a few hundred thousand in tied-up capital. It's not a one-off.

transcript.speaker: Marco Bell
transcript.text: And my engineers spend maybe a day a week just re-explaining what metrics mean. It's a tax on the whole team.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Understood. So there's hard cost in bad decisions and a soft cost in your engineers' time. If you fixed the literacy gap, what would good look like in six months?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Honestly, business teams self-serving the dashboards, asking better questions, and us not being a bottleneck. We'd measure it by fewer ad-hoc data requests and faster decision cycles.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Great — fewer ad-hoc requests and faster cycles are measurable, that helps. Have you tried to solve this before?

transcript.speaker: Marco Bell
transcript.text: We bought some generic online courses last year. Completion was about 15%. People didn't see how it applied to our data.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: So relevance and engagement were the killers. That's exactly where a tailored cohort program tends to win. Who else would need to be involved in evaluating something like this?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: I'd lead it, but our COO Janet sponsors anything that touches the broader org. Budget for L&D sits with her.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Makes sense. We can absolutely build a business case for Janet. What does a typical evaluation process look like for you — pilot first, or straight to a decision?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: We'd want a pilot. If it works with one or two teams we scale it. We're fairly quick once we see proof — weeks, not months.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll put together a pilot proposal scoped to two teams with success metrics tied to those ad-hoc request numbers. Does it make sense to get 30 minutes with Janet in the next couple of weeks?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raman
transcript.text: Yes, I can set that up. Send me the proposal and I'll loop her in.

transcript.speaker: Cameron Thody
transcript.text: Will do. Thanks both — I'll have the proposal over by Friday.
